# Lean vs. Haskell `malgo` runtime benchmark

**Historical.** Generated by `bash bench/lean-vs-haskell.sh` on 2026-07-18
(Darwin arm64). The script and the Haskell implementation it measured against
are both gone, and the trampoline (#360) has since changed the Zig backend's
calling convention, so these numbers describe neither implementation as it
stands. Kept as the last recorded comparison; see `PORTING.md`.
Fixture: `bench/fixtures/BenchFib.mlg` (naive recursive fib(15), un-memoized — a CPU-bound
workload; `examples/malgo/Fib.mlg` only computes fib(5), too small to
produce a stable wall-clock difference). `n = 15` (not larger) because
fib(18)/fib(20) reproducibly SIGSEGV when compiled via the Zig backend,
identically on both implementations — a pre-existing bug, not fixed here.

## `malgo eval` (small-step interpreter)

| Command | Mean [ms] | Min [ms] | Max [ms] | Relative |
|:---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `Haskell (eval)` | 359.3 ± 9.7 | 347.0 | 381.3 | 1.00 |
| `Lean (eval)` | 383.5 ± 8.3 | 364.9 | 391.8 | 1.07 ± 0.04 |

## `malgo compile --opt release-fast` (Zig backend, compiled binary)

| Command | Mean [ms] | Min [ms] | Max [ms] | Relative |
|:---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `Haskell-compiled` | 15.7 ± 2.9 | 9.4 | 24.3 | 1.07 ± 0.27 |
| `Lean-compiled` | 14.6 ± 2.6 | 9.0 | 25.9 | 1.00 |
